title: Replicas and a router: round robin, least outstanding, prefix affinity
goal: Run three model replicas and two gateways behind Nginx. The gateway routes each request with one of three policies and you measure the difference: prefix affinity sends requests that share a system prompt to the same replica, so llama.cpp reuses that prefix's KV cache instead of prefilling it again.

changes.note: Three policies; rendezvous hashing of the system prompt; bounded affinity; per-replica stats incl. prefix-cache hit ratio.
Route, then admit on that replica; spill to the next candidate once if it sheds; x-replica header.
L7 proxy for SSE: proxy_buffering off, long read timeout, no retries of POSTs, admin paths hidden.
nginx + gateway-a/b + llm-1/2/3; each gateway gets 2 of each replica's 4 slots.
60 requests over 3 long system prompts; prints TTFB percentiles and each gateway's per-replica stats.

run.label: Benchmark each policy in turn
run.cmd: for p in round_robin least_outstanding prefix_affinity; do ROUTER_POLICY=$p docker compose up -d gateway-a gateway-b; sleep 5; echo "== $p"; ./scripts/bench-routing.sh; done

verify.label: Two gateways answer through nginx
verify.cmd: for i in 1 2 3 4; do curl -s -o /dev/null -D - localhost:8080/v1/models | grep -i x-served-by; done
verify.expect: x-served-by alternates between gateway-a and gateway-b.

verify.label: Same system prompt, same replica
verify.cmd: for i in 1 2 3; do curl -s -o /dev/null -D - localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions -H 'authorization: Bearer sk-lab-acme-0001' -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a pirate."},{"role":"user","content":"Hi $i"}],"max_tokens":8}' | grep -i x-replica; done
verify.expect: Under prefix_affinity the same x-replica three times (whichever replica owns that prompt's hash).

verify.label: Compare the policies
verify.expect: Per-policy table: under prefix_affinity each prompt's requests concentrate on one replica and prefixHitRatio is high; under round_robin they spread and the ratio drops; TTFT p50 follows the hit ratio. If your llama.cpp build's timings lack cache_n, prefixHitRatio stays null: compare the TTFT percentiles instead.

verify.label: Admin paths are not public
verify.expect: 404 through nginx; JSON from the gateway's own port 8091.

concepts.how: Nginx balances at L7 (it parses HTTP, can route and log status codes); the gateway's router is a second, application-aware balancer.
Proxy buffering must be off for SSE, and the upstream keep-alive must outlive the proxy's.
Rendezvous hashing: removing a replica only moves the prompts it owned, unlike hash % N.
Prefix-aware routing with a load bound, exactly the score-cache-hits-minus-load idea in the lesson.
Prefix caching: reusing a prompt's KV cache skips its prefill, which is most of TTFT for long system prompts.
Stateless gateways scale out freely; the state that matters (KV caches) lives in the replicas, which is why routing matters.

checkpoints.text: nginx alternates between gateway-a and gateway-b; /admin is 404 through nginx.
Under prefix_affinity the same system prompt lands on the same replica.
I ran bench-routing.sh for all three policies and wrote down TTFT p50/p95 and prefixHitRatio for each.
I can explain why each gateway only gets 2 of each replica's 4 slots, and what that costs.
